name: [Portal] Portal localization CZ/SK/HU: screens, e-mails, validation, terms
description:
### Summary

The Partner Portal will launch in April 2027 to consulting agencies, freelancers, affiliate partners and addon developers in the Czech, Slovak and Hungarian markets, so every surface a partner meets must read naturally in Czech, Slovak and Hungarian, with English as a fallback where the codebase already provides it. This task is the cross-cutting localization pass over the whole portal: the shell, login, password recovery, registration, portal administrators, account settings and the medailonek editor, all transactional e-mails, validation and error messages, date, number and currency formats, the persisted per-user language choice, and language-aware links to the public partner websites and the terms page. It delivers an inventory of every string and e-mail, translation keys with no hardcoded text guarded by lint, complete translations, documented fallback behaviour when a key is missing, and an end-to-end smoke check per language. Translating partner-authored medailonek content and the marketing websites stays out of scope. The task depends on the portal screens being built first.

### Why?

The MVP opens to existing and new partners in CZ, SK and HU at the same time, so a portal that is complete only in Czech would exclude two of the three launch markets on day one. Each screen task adds its own strings and e-mails, and without a single owner of the language layer gaps, inconsistent terminology and untranslated fallbacks slip through unnoticed. Wiki Q7 explicitly leaves open what still has to be localized for CZ/SK/HU, and this task closes that question with a verified inventory rather than an assumption.

### What?

A partner who picks Czech, Slovak or Hungarian in account settings sees every portal screen, message and e-mail in that language, formatted with the matching date, number and currency conventions, and the choice survives across sessions and devices. Links to the public partner websites and to the terms (VOP) page lead to the version in the partner's language. When a translation is missing the portal shows a defined fallback instead of a raw key, and a lint or test guard stops new hardcoded strings from entering the codebase. An automated smoke run per language proves the main flows render correctly.

### Acceptance Criteria

An inventory of every user-facing string and transactional e-mail across all portal screens listed in Resources is attached to this issue; each entry maps to a translation key and no hardcoded user-facing text remains in Partner Portal PHP, React or Smarty code.

CZ, SK and HU translations exist for 100 % of inventoried keys and e-mail templates; EN is served only as fallback.

The language chosen in account settings is persisted per user and applied on the next login on any device; dates, times, numbers and currency amounts follow the selected locale on every portal screen.

Validation and error messages returned by backend endpoints and shown by portal forms are localized in all three languages.

Links to the public partner websites and to the terms (VOP) page resolve to the language matching the user's selection.

A missing key renders the documented fallback (EN, never a raw key) and is reported so it surfaces in review; a lint or test guard fails CI when a new hardcoded user-facing string is introduced in Partner Portal code.

Tests: new PHP passes PHPStan level 10; 

make fe-test

 covers the language switch and formatting helpers; an e2e smoke run per language (CZ, SK, HU) passes on login, shell, account settings and medailonek.

### Open questions

- Who supplies the SK and HU translations (Partnership, an internal localization team, or an agency) and by when relative to the Q4 2026 internal alpha?
- Wiki Q7: which URL per language does the terms link target, given the VOP text is managed in CRM by Partnership and public websites are still being decided (Wiki Q5)?
- Is EN a selectable UI language for the MVP or strictly a fallback? The wiki lists EN only in the long-term vision.
- Should e-mails follow the recipient's stored language or the language active in the session that triggered them (relevant for invitations sent by another administrator)?

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- React strings go through `useTranslation` from `admin/react/src/Core/translations/useTranslation.ts` (i18next; keys must be hard-coded, collected at build). Locales are configured in `admin/react/i18next-parser.config.ts` as `en_US, cs_CZ, hu_HU, sk_SK`; usage guide `admin/react/docs/translation-usage.md`.
- Catalogs are gettext `.po` files in `cms/langs/{cs_CZ,sk_SK,hu_HU,en_US}/LC_MESSAGES/translation.po`, bundled into React by `admin/react/build/vite-plugin-translations.ts`; Smarty e-mails in `admin/templates/emails/*.tpl` use `{t}…{/t}`.
- E-mail language is forced per message via `Localization::pretendFrontend` in `cms/packages/Email/SystemEmailBuilder.php` and `cms/packages/Email/ActionEmailBuilder.php`; per-user `language`, `dateFormat`, `timeFormat` live on `cms/packages/Profiles/Model/AdminUser.php`.
- Date/time/number formatting context: `admin/react/src/Core/context/Localization/LocalizationProvider.tsx` (wraps `@shoptet/ui` `LocalizationProvider` with locale, dateFormat, timeFormat, timezones).
- No hardcoded-string lint exists yet: `admin/react/eslint.config.mjs` only restricts direct `react-i18next` imports; the guard is new work. CODEOWNERS: `admin/react/src/PartnerPortal/**` → `@shoptet/devrel-team`, `*.tsx` → `@shoptet/frontend-team`.
